Subject: April 1, 2022 to March 31, 2023 ASC 712 Expense Results
KeySpan 
Enclosed is the fiscal year 2023 ASC 712 expense valuation for KeySpan. The valuation is based on 
January 1, 2022 data provided by National Grid. Based on a 3.35 percent discount rate assumption, 
the incremental operating income for the period April 1, 2022 through March 31, 2023 is $3.0 million. 
Fiscal Year 2023 Valuation Results 
The 
2023 was more favorable than budgeted. In aggregate, 
March 31, 2022 liability was $0.9 million lower than expected. 
The key items that impacted the liability included: 
A change in discount rate from 2.25% to 3.35%, 
Higher than expected number of terminations and recoveries, 
Favorable claims experience and trend assumption; offset by 
liabilities 
Enclosed is a summary of expense/(income) by business unit, as well as a summary of the 
assumptions and benefit provisions used in the valuation.

Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2023. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein. 
In conducting the valuation, we have relied on personnel, plan design and health care claim cost 
supplied by National Grid. While we cannot verify the accuracy of all of the supplied information, the 
information was reviewed for consistency and reasonability. As a result of this review, we have no 
reason to doubt the substantial accuracy or completeness of the information and believe that it has 
produced appropriate results. 
This valuation has been conducted in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles and 
practices, including the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice as issued by the Actuarial 
Standards Board. In addition, the valuation results are based on our understanding of the 
requirements of ASC 712-10. The information in this report is not intended to supersede or supplant 
the advice and interpretations 
The actuarial assumptions and methods used in this valuation are described in the ASC 712 
Assumptions and Methods section. National Grid selected the economic, demographic, and health 
care claims cost assumptions and prescribed them for use for purposes of compliance with ASC 712-
10. Aon provided guidance with respect to these assumptions, and it is our belief that they represent
reasonable expectations of anticipated plan experience. The actuarial cost method is prescribed by
ASC 712-10.
A valuation model was used to develop the liabilities for the March 31, 2022 valuation. The valuation 
model relies on ProVal software, which was developed by Winklevoss Technologies, LLC. Experts 
within Aon selected this software and determined it is appropriate for performing valuations. We 
coded and reviewed the software for the provisions, assumptions, methods, and data of the specific 
for this arrangement. The undersigned relied on experts at Aon for the development of the capital 
market assumptions models underlying the discount rate.  
Models are used to estimate underlying per capita medical, prescription drug and dental claims costs 
and plan design actuarial values, subsequently utilized as assumption inputs for valuation models 
used to develop the liabilities for the 2022 and future valuations. The models used for the 
development of plan design actuarial values were developed by experts outside of Aon, specifically 
Optum. The Aon consulting team leveraged expertise of Health experts within Aon as it relates to 
reviewing the models developed by experts outside of Aon, and those used for development of the 
per capita claims costs and future trend rates. 
In addition to the valuation model, results rely on a custom Microsoft Excel model to develop the 
IBNR liability. The model was developed and reviewed by Aon LTD team members and evaluated as 
appropriate for performing IBNR calculations.

Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2023. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein. 
In conducting the valuation, we have relied on personnel, plan design and health care claim cost 
supplied by National Grid. While we cannot verify the accuracy of all of the supplied information, the 
information was reviewed for consistency and reasonability. As a result of this review, we have no 
reason to doubt the substantial accuracy or completeness of the information and believe that it has 
produced appropriate results. 
This valuation has been conducted in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles and 
practices, including the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice as issued by the Actuarial 
Standards Board. In addition, the valuation results are based on our understanding of the 
requirements of ASC 712-10. The information in this report is not intended to supersede or supplant 
 
The actuarial assumptions and methods used in this valuation are described in the ASC 712 
Assumptions and Methods section. National Grid selected the economic, demographic, and health 
care claims cost assumptions and prescribed them for use for purposes of compliance with ASC 712-
10. Aon provided guidance with respect to these assumptions, and it is our belief that they represent 
reasonable expectations of anticipated plan experience. The actuarial cost method is prescribed by 
ASC 712-10. 
A valuation model was used to develop the liabilities for the March 31, 2022 valuation. The valuation 
model relies on ProVal software, which was developed by Winklevoss Technologies, LLC. Experts 
within Aon selected this software and determined it is appropriate for performing valuations. We 
coded and reviewed the software for the provisions, assumptions, methods, and data of the specific 
for this arrangement. The undersigned relied on experts at Aon for the development of the capital 
market assumptions models underlying the discount rate.  
Models are used to estimate underlying per capita medical and prescription drug claims costs, 
subsequently utilized as assumption inputs for valuation models used to develop the liabilities for the 
2022 and future valuations. The Aon consulting team leveraged expertise of Health experts within 
Aon as it relates to reviewing the models used for the development of the per capita claims costs and 
future trend rates. 
In addition to the valuation model, results rely on a custom Microsoft Excel model to develop the 
IBNR liability. The model was developed and reviewed by Aon LTD team members and evaluated as 
appropriate for performing IBNR calculations.

Customer Zero Based Redesign (ZBR)
Drive Paperless Adoption
Customer
KEDY, KEDLI, and NMPC
This initiative reflects the paperless bill credit provided to customers who convert from paper to electronic billing.  The credit is based on Historic Test Year costs and represents the difference in cost to produce a paper bill versus producing an electronic bill.  
Savings achieved by the Company (i.e., the cost of envelopes, paper, postage, and processing – less the cost to provide an electronic bill), would be returned to electronically billed customers in the form of a credit on each bill.  For revenue requirement purposes, 
the program is cost and revenue neutral.
The HTY reflects $0.377 million and $0.612 million in savings for KEDLI and KEDNY respectively, with additional savings of $0.104 million for KEDLI and $0.169 million for KEDNY forecast in the Rate Year (as shown below).  The total cumulative savings of $0.481 
million and $0.781 million for KEDLI and KEDNY, respectively, is equal to the credit given to customers switching to an electronic bill under the tariffs.
The Rate Year forecast costs to achieve these savings are $0.033 million for KEDLI and $0.071 million for KEDNY.

Uncontrolled Locks ‐ Blended Crews
Gas
KEDNY
Certain work that requires access to the curb valve (e.g., collections, inactive accounts, new accounts, etc.) utilize Gas Field Operations (“GFO”) resources such as trucks and two‐man crews.  With the primary duty of GFO’s resources being to use a compressor 
to blow out debris to access the curb valve, there is an opportunity to shift resources to Customer Meter Services (“CMS”) and decrease costs associated with curb valve blow‐outs.  This initiative involves a blended crew approach of GFO and CMS resources to 
minimize repeat visits, resulting in reduced costs, lower emissions, and enhanced customer satisfaction.
This is a KEDNY only initiative.  The HTY reflects $0.264 million in savings, with additional savings of $0.028 million forecast in the Rate Year (as shown below).  The total cumulative savings from this initiative is $0.292 million.

GBE (Gas Business Enablement)
Summons Reductions
Gas
NMPC, KEDNY
These four initiatives (PRJ‐1930, PRJ‐1931, PRJ‐1913, and PRJ‐1933) have been enabled through the GBE program.  Specifically, they result from digital enhancements made possible by the common work, asset management, and scheduling systems delivered by 
the GBE program.  The program allows the Company to better bundle together work thereby optimizing scheduling/dispatching, which in turn, results in lower labor costs, lesser truck rolls, and improved satisfaction.  Lower truck rolls also contribute to reduced 
emissions.  For example, before GBE, the Company may have sent a technician to a home to repair a device on the meter.  Unknown at the time, however, because of the disparate systems, that customer could have been scheduled for a meter replacement six 
months later.  
For PRJ‐1913, the savings in the HTY of $1.742 million is more than what the Company forecasts for the Rate Year ($1.100 million).  For revenue requirement purposes, the Company reflected the HTY amount and did not make a normalizing adjustment to lower 
those savings.

Supply Chain Optimization
Supply Chain Sourcing and Contract Management
Gas
KEDNY, KEDLI, NMPC
Supply Chain Optimization is not an initiative per se.  Rather, Supply Chain Optimization captures the summary results of Procurement’s execution of sourcing and contract management activities completed in conjunction with the businesses.  Specifically, 
included within the line item is multiple contract revisions/updates executed by Procurement that have resulted in one‐time cost reductions over the term of the new or updated contract along with other strategic sourcing efforts to lower costs.  
Procurement manages a list of opportunities, tracks their progress, and reviews the outcomes.  This underlying list informs an aggregate forecast and overall achieved savings that is ultimately reflected in the summary Supply Chain Optimization project.  
The list may include aspirational and/or immature opportunities which can be identified via the status/progress level assigned by Procurement.  
The HTY reflects $5.975 million and $6.192 million in savings for KEDLI and KEDNY, respectively, with additional savings of $1.517 million for KEDLI and $2.282 million for KEDNY forecast in the Rate Year.  The total cumulative savings from this initiative is 
$7.492 million and $8.451 million for KEDLI and KEDNY, respectively.
